item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Meh. I find myself extremely uninterested in this one. It attempts several things done better elsewhere and mentioned earlier in the comments. It just doesn't compel me to feel much of anything at all. The ship isn't interesting, it's just a broken down ship. Sure, no records of the thing, but that's not really enough to catch my interest, it's been done and could even happen by mundane means, under some circumstances. And sure, there's a brain-nerve monster thing shoved in there to make anyone nearby spontaneously run over for the Sahara lobotomy special, but again, I find myself asking, so? We are told little to nothing about it, other than it'll dead you.

It feels like someone taped these two barely started SCP concepts together and called it done. There isn't any particular reason for the brain thing to be in the ship, as well, I'd actually find it more compelling if it was sitting out in the middle of the desert with no protection from the elements and was still doing its brain-grabbin thing. Even then, this would cry out for really any sort of substantive narrative. Down voted.

The latitude and longitude are said to be "approximate", but are given down to the nearest 0.01 arcseconds, which is under a meter, much less than the size of a ship. ██° ██' ██" would be much more reasonable than ██° ██' ██.██" in my opinion.

"consistent to exposure" should be "consistent with exposure".

It's a weird thing that makes you go to it and then you die. SCP-162 did it better.

item.content:encoded:
As one could glean from the fact I have just downvoted this article, I am not a fan. Although the ship itself isn't bad and the nerve cluster feels it could be made good with more work, having the two in the same article feels as if someone had crammed two SCPs together without thinking much about their connection. Specifically speaking, on one hand one could have pretty much any SCP on board of the ship and it wouldn't change much (indeed, early revisions pretty much had a different SCP), and on the other we've got no clue as to why this ship has allegedly never been built or why it ended up in the middle of the Sahara Desert.

And don't even get me started on the compulsion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Because Telekil is a limited substance and was abused by writers since it was posted as an automatic addition in many containment schemes. We've shied away from using it more recently and generally suggest that new authors do not. Additionally, it leads to a form of highly generic cross referencing in articles. Similar problems have occurred with suggestion the destruction of 682 with an object, putting something through 914, using 500 as an answer, etc. As a general rule, it's never a good idea to blithely mention another SCP in one's own article, merely for the sake of mentioning it.

Personally, I like to think that we're simply "out" of telekil, that the substance is spread too thin around the Foundation for us to use it anywhere else, and our scientists are unable to replicate the effect.

item.title: What we thought up in the chat
item.content:encoded:
As in title, we thought up this so far (i'll edit this post when something new pops up):

  • No ball of nerves thingy anymore
  • The ship doesn't assimilate no one
  • The ship was/is a petroleum ship
  • The shadows of the ship depict a non-derelict petroleum ship with a crew that does whatever a crew does
  • The ship "sails" periodically for petroleum-rich deposits in the desert, and stays there for a bit. The shadow "drills" the deposit and sucks up … shadow petroleum, i guess.
  • The ship, with the cargo "full" of shadow petroleum then goes to deposit it to a port, possibly a port that was but isn't there anymore. We're working on this bit.
  • The involvement of the Foundation is simply to limit the damage on the people that find themselves on the ship path: the vessel "crew" is completely oblivious to villages and whatnot. We can do this by tampering the on-board equipment (compass, GPS, gyros, who knows) or the rudder. Or by organizing a MTF to simulate a Greenpeace attack on the ship, while on a Greenpeace boat, mounted on a camouflaged tank, on the desert. Who knows, we need to get creative. Still working on this too.
  • Also, we might use the ship ability to find petroleum to organize nearly 100% successful oil drilling operations.

I believe the core idea has a great potential, also, the pic is fantastic.
So, i'll upvote this on faith! Keep up the good work!

Having a remote-recon drone uncover the fact that nerve tissue is not simply removed but transported into some grotesque gestalt growing within the SCP or something creepy and "wrong" to that effect might give it the punch it needs.
